messages:
maria: Heads up — saw KMS decrypts in the audit log that don't line up with org ownership. Decrypts for project `proj-42` show up under org `org-beta` but workspace belongs to `org-alpha`. Possible alias reuse? :thinking:
ken: Can you paste the raw log lines? are these `kms:decrypt` events or app-level logs?
maria: It's `KMS:Decrypt` entries. snippet: ```json
{"time":"2026-03-19T14:02:12Z","principal":"service-account@org-beta","key_alias":"alias/redwood-project-42"}
``` Looks like alias shared across two orgs.
jess: @maria thanks — if key aliases aren't globally namespaced that sounds like a naming/mapping bug. @rick can the binding code validate key ownership by org?
rick: Investigating. Our KMS naming used `alias/<project_id>` which assumed project IDs are globally unique. They are not — we missed the org prefix on import.
sara: We ran a migration last week that accepted legacy `proj-*` ids from S3 manifests. That migration could have created duplicate project ids across orgs. Triage suggestion: stop allowing decrypts for ambiguous aliases and revoke the binding.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1124 "kms-tenant-alias-conflict" — paging oncall @pagerduty
ken: Quick mitigation: add a runtime check to verify `key.owner_org_id == request.org_id` before allowing decrypt. Someone take a PR for a hotfix? Need this in 30m.
rick: On it. I’ll push a canary that reads owner metadata from the key vault and returns 403 on mismatch.
jess: Also we should enrich audit logs to include `resolved_key_id` (the canonical KMS uuid) rather than just alias so future forensics don't rely on aliases. Add an eval for that.
alicia: If any customer data was exposed cross-org we may have a reporting obligation. Please quantify scope and notify me immediately with affected account IDs.
maria: Initial scan: 12 decrypt events across 3 customers. Two appear to be infra telemetry, one looks like an actual user data decrypt. Putting details into secure ticket now.
rick: PR posted: platform#5432 — adds org ownership check and switches resolution to canonical key id. Rolling to canary in us-west-2. ETA ~18m.
sara: Canary shows 403s for org mismatches and blocked ~10 suspicious decrypts. If no false positives, we’ll roll global after 30m.
jess: Solid. Postmortem owners: @jess (sec), @rick (eng-platform), @sara (infra). Include timeline, root cause = non-globally-namespaced project ids + alias-based resolution, mitigations, and compensating controls.
ken: :thumbsup: Please also add unit tests and update the key-import docs to mandate `org-<id>` prefix for project ids.
maria: I'll follow up in the secure ticket with the export of the single customer event and notify the affected account rep. :warning:
